name: masters-pods-shelf/strip-a
refs: THE LAYOUT (a flat wireframe, project-owned): the exact horizontal bands, edge to edge. From the top: cream plaster; a long dark umber wood back-board; a lighter wood shelf ledge under it with a thin shadow; cream plaster; and at the bottom the top of the next identical board. Keep these band heights and positions exactly. Never copy its flat look.

THE WOOD AND PLASTER (our signed concept, project-owned): copy this aged, polished umber wood, its grain and its matte painted finish, and the soft cream plaster wall. Do NOT copy the round niches, the pods, the rings, the glow, the star or the small name plaques: none of them appear in the new picture.

THE PAINTED LANGUAGE (one of our signed room paintings, project-owned): its matte painterly miniature rendering, soft occlusion, warm golden key light from the upper left and cosy palette. Take the treatment and the warmth only.
prompt:
Paint a texture strip for a game screen, seen perfectly front-on and flat (orthographic, no perspective, no vanishing point): one section of a naturalist's cabinet in a warm home, made of horizontal bands that run unbroken across the full width, exactly as the layout gives them. From top to bottom: (1) a band of soft warm cream plaster wall; (2) a long back-board of aged umber wood, its grain running horizontally, plain and quiet, no knots, no nails, no holes, no niches, no carving, no plaques; (3) under it a slightly lighter wood shelf ledge, its top lip catching the light, its front face a plain plank; (4) a soft shadow cast by the ledge onto the plaster just below it, then plain cream plaster; (5) at the very bottom, the top of the next identical back-board.

This strip will be repeated vertically, so: the light is the SAME at the top and the bottom of the picture (no vertical gradient, no vignette, no darkening toward any edge); the plaster is a quiet even surface with only a faint hand-trowelled texture, a few hairline cracks at most, no stones, no moss, no stains. Warm lantern light comes from the left: the left side is a little warmer and brighter, falling off gently toward the right, the same at every height.

The picture is completely EMPTY: no objects, no pods, no niches, no holes, no rings, no lamp, no plants, no labels, no text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no frame, no border. Matte, hand-painted miniature finish, low saturation umber and cream, never bright orange, no gloss, no chrome, no plastic.
